papers.title: Weak-field multi-collector benchmark
papers.hypothesis: A frozen local-flow policy has a finite grid-censored positive matched first-interception boundary under the primary uniform-field condition.
papers.kill_criterion: Stop or narrow if the oracle cannot exploit the field, exact counterfactual matching fails, or passive and swept-area controls explain the effect.
papers.open_blocker: Event-keyed tie breaking, within-step continuous contact or timestep convergence, matched-pair episode wrapper, and frozen local_flow_v1 remain incomplete; growing geometry is not primary-ready.

papers.title: Inactive placeholder
papers.kill_criterion: No second paper may activate without a genuinely separable question and Program Director decision.

primary_question: What is the weakest latent-field signal strength at which a team of locally observing collectors achieves a reliably positive matched improvement in pre-contact first-interception performance over otherwise identical no-signal episodes?

engineering_tests.scope: simulation primitives, collector dynamics, deterministic reset, causal local observations, minimal environment, smoke policies, trajectory schemas, and limiting cases

fresh_review.strongest_new_threat: Endpoint-only capture can miss within-step crossings and move the primary first-contact outcome.
